sections.text: My name is Jiří Gottwald and I have worked in electronics and electrical engineering on the Czech market for 25 years. In 2010, I began expanding my portfolio to include photovoltaic systems.

items.title: Read more
items.text:
Since our first installation, we have come a long way together and learned a great deal. Our goal has always been the same: to provide customers with the highest quality and the most honest service. After careful, long-term testing, we therefore selected reliable photovoltaic systems from ALPHA ESS and Wattsonic. These are innovative systems for storing and using photovoltaic energy.

Our commitment to quality and honest work has paid off.

I invited my son to join the family business and am gradually passing on my years of know-how. We continue to improve and look for new solutions in home energy. We can connect heat pumps which, through their distinctive integration with photovoltaics, can be controlled using smart devices to maximise the use of generated energy. Together, the heat pump, photovoltaics and our smart home form a distinctive ecosystem that helps you achieve greater self-sufficiency and efficiency.

sections.title: Gottwald – a home photovoltaic system for domestic hot water.
How does photovoltaics work?
sections.text:
The photovoltaic installation is not connected to the distribution grid; the required number of photovoltaic panels is simply installed on your roof.

The electricity generated is carried by cables to a controller, which distributes it to the water heater’s heating element. The controller also ensures optimum use of the energy from the solar panels and supplements it from the grid if there is insufficient output. The photovoltaic system is safe and highly reliable.

sections.title: Benefits of the photovoltaic system
sections.text:
Installation does not require complicated building alterations

Photovoltaic panels generate energy even in overcast weather

The panels do not overheat and do not need liquid cooling

sections.title: Why choose our photovoltaics?
sections.text:
Our company, GottSol, offers proven, technologically advanced NECTARSUN equipment for photovoltaic water heating.

Combined with a controller featuring MPPT, power generated by the panels can be combined with electricity from the grid, with priority always given to electricity from your photovoltaic system.

A fully automatic system compatible with most common water heaters

Control via a simple app

sections.title: Panel safety shutdown with monitoring: TIGO TS4-A-0
sections.text:
An optimiser is fitted to each individual panel. It can measure that panel’s output and disconnect it from generation in an emergency.

Individual outputs can be monitored in the app

These optimisers must be supplemented with TIGO Cloud Connect Advanced (CCA) and, at certain distances, a Tigo Access Point (TAP)

sections.title: Panel safety shutdown without monitoring: TIGO TS-A-2F
sections.text:
This optimiser connects two panels, which it can disconnect from generation in an emergency.

Each string must be supplemented with a TIGO RSS transmitter, which sends a signal through the DC cables to enable the optimisers to generate power.

sections.title: SPLIT heat pump
sections.text:
A modern split heat pump has separate outdoor and indoor units. These two main parts are connected by a refrigerant circuit and a communication cable.

The heat pump is designed for heating, cooling and, where required, domestic hot water. The indoor unit is fully equipped for connection to an indirectly heated hot-water cylinder. The outdoor unit also comes with an outdoor temperature sensor fitted at the factory. If the location of the outdoor unit prevents accurate measurement of outdoor temperature, another optional outdoor sensor can easily be connected. And that is not all!

Advanced electronics regulate not only the hot-water circuit, but also the direct and mixed zones of the heating circuit. Cooling mode is also available in the summer.

An air-to-water heat pump with the highest efficiency on the market (COP 4.61 at A2/W35 – EN 14511)

Inverter technology patented for R290 refrigerant

High outlet temperature of up to 70 °C

Ideal for heating-system renovations

Quiet operation, with a minimum sound pressure level of 44 dB(A)

A high-quality, robust construction provides an above-average service life

5-year warranty

Servicing directly from the manufacturer

Control via a mobile app

sections.title: How a split air-to-water heat pump works
sections.text: A split heat pump consists of two main parts: an outdoor unit and an indoor unit. The two units are connected by a refrigerant circuit and a communication cable.

image.alt: How a split air-to-water heat pump works

sections.title: Main components of the outdoor unit
sections.text: An evaporator, two fans with EC motors, a rotary compressor, an electronic expansion valve, a four-way valve and control electronics.

sections.title: Components of the indoor unit
sections.text:
A condenser, circulation pump, control electronics, connection terminals and a control panel for setting and regulating the entire heat pump.

An air-to-water heat pump takes heat from the outdoor environment and transfers it to the refrigerant in the evaporator. The higher air temperature causes the refrigerant to evaporate, and the vapour is drawn into the compressor. The compressor rapidly compresses the refrigerant vapour, significantly increasing its temperature through this simple physical process. The hot vapour transfers its heat to the heating water in the condenser (a plate heat exchanger in the indoor unit), losing its energy and changing from a gas to a liquid.

The liquid refrigerant flows from the condenser to the outdoor unit, where the expansion valve sharply reduces its pressure and cools it significantly. The cycle closes as the refrigerant returns to the evaporator, where it is heated by the air again. This process repeats continuously, moving heat from the outside environment into the heating system.

sections.title: MONOBLOCK heat pump
sections.text:
A monoblock heat pump has an outdoor unit fully equipped with both a refrigerant circuit and a heating circuit. It is designed for heating, cooling and, where required, domestic hot water. Because the heating circuit runs directly from the building to the heat pump, the unit must be protected against the heating water freezing.

The heat pump comes with an outdoor temperature sensor fitted at the factory.

A modern room controller is also supplied as standard. Advanced electronics regulate the hot-water circuit and the direct and mixed zones of the heating circuit, as well as up to six heat pumps in a cascade without a higher-level controller. All of this is handled by the control unit supplied as standard with the heat pump! Cooling mode is also available in summer.

Continuously variable output thanks to inverter technology

The lowest heat-pump noise on the market (quieter than a whisper), with a minimum sound pressure level of 35 dB(A)

The latest technology built into the heat pump (radial fan)

Heating, hot water and cooling in one device

Control via the internet and a mobile app

LWAV + – a version with air ducts for even quieter operation

sections.title: How does a heat pump work?
sections.text:
A heat pump takes heat from the surroundings of the heated building (air, ground or water) and raises it to a temperature suitable for heating and domestic hot water.

A heat pump can use this principle to obtain free heat from its surroundings. How can it obtain heat from somewhere cold? By cooling that place even further and taking heat from it. This principle allows a heat pump to extract heat even from air at −20 °C. Extracting heat at such low temperatures is slightly less efficient, but still beneficial.

sections.title: What are the advantages of SPLIT and MONOBLOCK systems?
sections.text:
1. SPLIT heat pumps have separate outdoor (heat exchanger) and indoor units, connected by refrigerant piping.

Advantages:

No risk of the system freezing

A small, lightweight outdoor unit

Disadvantages:

More space required indoors for the indoor unit

Regular professional checks of the refrigerant system

2. MONOBLOCK heat pumps have a single outdoor unit containing everything required. It is simply connected to the existing water system.

No indoor space needs to be allocated

The refrigerant circuit is hermetically sealed in the outdoor unit

A greater risk of freezing compared with SPLIT

sections.title: Nová zelená úsporám subsidy programme
sections.text: Nová zelená úsporám is one of the most effective programmes in the Czech Republic focused on energy savings. Customers who choose to install photovoltaics at home can receive a state contribution of up to CZK 140,000.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.text:
Owners of existing houses used as permanent residences

Owners of individually defined residential units arranged in a row (terraced houses)

Public-benefit organisations established by local authorities

sections.title: Subsidy amounts for photovoltaic systems
sections.text:
For each 1 kWp of installed output – CZK 10,000

For each 1 kWh of electricity storage – CZK 10,000

Maximum subsidy for output and storage – CZK 100,000

Bonus for intelligent control and sharing – CZK 40,000

sections.title: Who guarantees that I will receive a subsidy?
sections.text:
It is important to understand that anyone who meets the conditions of the Nová zelená úsporám (NZÚ) programme is entitled to the subsidy.

Before installation, we apply to the State Environmental Fund (SFŽP) for approval of the subsidy for your property and a guarantee of payment to your account.

The SFŽP provides the payment guarantee once all conditions have been met.

sections.title: When is the subsidy paid?
sections.text:
The subsidy is paid once the system is fully connected to the distribution grid.

The distribution technician carrying out the connection and inspection issues a document on the basis of which payment can be requested.

Payment takes approximately one month from the issue of that document.
